summary: Soiku Shigematsu specializes in Buddhist studies and English literature, having studied at TUFS, University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, and under Kiju Shigematsu. He held posts at Shizuoka Women's University, Shizuoka University (1975–2001), and Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).

Sojo Hirano was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and as shike at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996). He taught Sonja Arntzen and Yoel Hoffmann.

Sokatsu Shaku worked in Buddhist studies, studying under traditional teachers Kōsen Imakita (1889) and Soyen Shaku (1893–1898). He founded Ryobokai, Ryobokai Dojo of North America, and Ningen Zen, and taught Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki, Zuigan Goto, and Eizan Tatsuta.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tokyo University of the Arts/Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts, California Institute of the Arts, San Francisco Art Institute, and under Sokatsu Shaku and Soyen Shaku. He founded the First Zen Institute of America.

Sokichi Tsuda was a scholar of history, sinology, and Japanology who studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō. He worked at the SMR Research Department (~1908–1919), University of Tokyo (~1920–1923), and Waseda University (~1918–1940), which he founded in 1935.

Soko Morinaga worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Toyama High School, Daitoku-ji, and under Sesso Oda and Zuigan Goto. He served as abbot at Daishuin (~1963–1995) and head of Hanazono University (1986–1994).

Sokuo Eto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and the University of Tokyo. He founded Dokenryo (1937) and served as president of Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1958) and professor at Komazawa University (1953).

Solomon Caesar Malan was an Indologist and linguist educated at St Edmund Hall, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh. He held positions at Bishop's College, Calcutta (1838), The Asiatic Society (~1838–1840), and Balliol College, Oxford (1843).

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who earned a doctorate from the University of Oxford. He has served as a departmental lecturer at Oxford and a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2019).
Soma Thera was a Buddhist studies figure who was educated at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and studied under Jetavana Sayadaw. He was also a member of Servants of the Buddha (~1928–1936).

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held appointments at the French Institute of Pondicherry, Wolfson College, Oxford, Clay Sanskrit Library, Kyoto University, and Columbia University.

Somboon Watana works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Panjab University in 1999 under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma, and became an assistant professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Madras. He served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara and under Swami Satyananda Puri and Vajirayanavangsa. He served as director at Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961) and abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013).
Somphong Santacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

Somsak Phansiri specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Madras (2005–2011) and served as a lecturer at Buriram Rajabhat University (2026).

Sonam Chhoki is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who earned an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London. She worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Choden is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies researcher. Attested in 2026, she studied as a Doctoral Local Researcher at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin.

Sonam Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko (~1961–1967), taught Shinjo Kawasaki, and served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

Sonam Jamtsho works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he studied as a Doctoral Local Researcher at the University of Hamburg, served there as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter, and taught Gembo Dorji.
